video_title: Home Prices Set To Slide 30% | Nick Gerli
gist: Housing analyst Nick Gerli (Reventure) argues the US is in a fourth-year housing 'demand depression' with sales below 2008 levels, rising Sun Belt/Western inventory and fading rate lock-in, forecasting a slow price grind lower in WA, CO, TN, TX, AZ and FL in 2027 while AI-driven agglomeration lifts New York, Chicago and San Francisco, with Manhattan his top buy. The title's '30% slide' reflects his claim that prices would be 20-30% lower in a normally functioning market, not his base-case 12-month forecast (single-digit declines); he adds a demographic cliff (deaths exceeding births by ~2030-2034) that is especially bearish for Florida retirement markets.

insights.claim: US housing demand is in its fourth year of a 'demand depression': pending sales, mortgage purchase applications and existing sales are below 2008-09 levels despite ~4% unemployment (vs 10% then); adjusted for population and housing stock, Gerli calls it the worst demand period in US history.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Housing transaction-volume-dependent businesses (brokers, mortgage originators, title) face a depressed base with no cyclical rebound yet.
insights.quote: When you adjust for the population in the housing stock, this is actually the the worst period we've ever had for demand in US history.

insights.claim: Mortgage purchase applications were down 15-16% year-over-year through mid-October 2026, signaling that home sales will weaken further into late 2026/2027.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Leading indicator points to further declines in existing sales and mortgage origination volume.

insights.claim: National inventory is within ~5% of its 2019 level, and supply in the South and West is at a 10-year high, contradicting the 'locked-up market / 3% rate lock-in' narrative of low supply.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Supply normalization removes the main pillar of the 'prices can't fall' thesis in Sun Belt/Western markets.

insights.claim: Gerli argues demand is not returning as inventory rises, which disproves the industry claim that low demand was caused by low inventory; the real cause is unaffordability (high prices plus ~7% rates) compounded by white-collar job insecurity.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Rising listings will not unlock volume without price cuts; expect price to be the adjustment variable.
insights.quote: They tried to tell us, "Oh, the only reason demand is low is because inventory is low." Fast forward to late 2026, inventory is skyrocketing and demand keeps dropping.

insights.claim: National home prices are roughly flat year-over-year (Zillow) or up ~1% (NAR), but national averages mask declines in about half the country because the Northeast and Midwest still have shortages.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: National HPI is a misleading signal; regional exposure determines outcomes for mortgage credit, builders and REITs.

insights.claim: NAR's September 2026 data show $1M+ single-family sales up 4% YoY while every lower bucket fell ($0-100k -8%, $100-250k -7%, $250-500k -3%, $500-750k -1%), meaning a mix shift toward wealthy buyers is inflating national median prices.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Median price stats overstate housing health; underlying like-for-like values are weaker than headlines.
insights.quote: 1 million plus up 4% year-over-year. Every other bucket 0 to 100 down 8%.

insights.claim: US homebuilder sentiment sank to its lowest reading since June 2012 (a 14-year low); 43% of builders cut prices in October (highest share since 2020), about two-thirds used incentives, and buyer traffic fell five points to 18, near 2008 levels.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Homebuilder margins are under pressure from price cuts and incentives; builder equities face earnings risk.

insights.claim: Gerli views 7% mortgage rates (30-year fixed at ~7.4-7.5% now) as historically normal, below the 1970s-90s (8-9% in the 1990s), so the path of least resistance to restore affordability is falling prices, not lower rates.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Do not count on rate relief to rescue housing; price declines are the likely clearing mechanism.
insights.quote: mortgage rates at 7% are abundantly normal.

insights.claim: Values have already fallen sharply over four years in many Sun Belt/Western metros: Austin -27%, Punta Gorda -22%, Cape Coral-Fort Myers -17%, North Port-Sarasota -15%, New Orleans -12%, Phoenix -11%, and San Antonio, Boulder, Naples, Stockton, Denver around -9% (expected to reach -10% soon); Boise -7.6%, Dallas -7.4%.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Pandemic boomtowns are in an established downtrend; lenders and investors with Sun Belt concentration face mark-downs.

insights.claim: On-the-ground, Gerli is finding individual houses in Las Vegas, Dallas and Florida selling $100k-$200k below their peak sale price, suggesting aggregate statistics will worsen in those markets.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Transaction-level losses lead index data; expect index declines to widen.

insights.claim: Reventure's base-case 12-month forecast (to Sept 2027, no recession assumed) has Washington -6.7% (weakest), Colorado -6%, Tennessee -5.9%, Utah -4.9%, Arizona -4.6%, Texas -4.3%, Florida -3%, while Connecticut +5.9%, Illinois +5.3%, New Jersey +3.4% and New York +3.1%.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Provides a state-level long/short map for housing-exposed assets: weak West/Sun Belt, firm Northeast/Midwest.

insights.claim: Colorado inventory hit 34,000 homes in September versus a normal ~22,000 (nearly tripled over five years) while sales volume is at a 12-year low.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Supply glut with collapsing demand points to continued price declines in Colorado.

insights.claim: In Denver the mortgage payment (incl. tax and insurance) still consumes ~40% of a $117k median income versus a 33% long-term average and 23% after the last crash, despite prices falling only 9% in four years, implying substantially more downside.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
entities: mortgage payment as a percentage of income
insights.so_what: Payment-to-income gap versus history quantifies how far prices must fall to restore affordability.

insights.claim: Some markets are booming: San Francisco County values are up 15% YoY, Fairfield County CT and Westchester County NY are up close to double digits, and New York City is turning up; Reventure forecasts 6-7% gains for many NYC suburbs.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Housing exposure tied to AI/finance hubs is outperforming; regional bifurcation is a trade.

insights.claim: Illinois is among the strongest forecast states (Cook County +6.1%, Lake County +7.4%, DuPage +6.1%) because it builds almost no homes (permits ~0.33% of stock, second-lowest after Alaska, roughly one-fifth of Florida's rate), domestic out-migration shrank to ~40,000 in 2025 (best in 35 years), and it is only ~3.9% overvalued.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Low-supply, fairly-valued Midwest markets can appreciate even without boom-level demand.

insights.claim: Chicago metro inventory fell from about 40,000 homes for sale in September 2019 to about 16,000 now, a genuine shortage; north-side Chicago values are already up ~12.5% over 12 months.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Chicago is a legitimate shortage market where the mainstream 'low supply' narrative actually holds.

insights.claim: Hyper-local divergence matters: in Dallas, Reventure forecasts -8% to -9% in southern/eastern/western areas while Highland Park and University Park are forecast to rise, so buyers in Mesquite should bid below list while Highland Park buyers should expect bidding wars.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Zip-code-level analysis beats metro averages for underwriting residential exposure.

insights.claim: Adjusted for inflation, the counties with the highest real appreciation (parts of Tennessee, Utah, upstate New York, Indiana and Washington) carry the most potential downside.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Screens for downside risk by real appreciation rather than nominal gains.

themes.theme: Seller Denial and Rate Lock-In Erosion

insights.claim: Gerli's base case for 2027 is a slow grind down in prices rather than a waterfall, because sellers anchored to four-year-old comps and 3% mortgages only capitulate after months of unsold listings, rejected offers and relisting; a recession plus stock market correction would rapidly accelerate the decline.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Expect gradual price erosion absent a macro shock; a recession is the trigger for a faster correction.
insights.quote: that will pierce the delusion very quickly in a lot of these sellers minds.

insights.claim: Per Fannie Mae data, the share of mortgage holders with 6%+ rates now exceeds those with sub-3% rates (as of Q2 2026), flipped from March 2022 when 25% were sub-3% and only 7% were 6%+; the shift will accelerate the longer rates stay high.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Rate lock-in is fading as a supply constraint, so more owners will list at market-clearing prices.

insights.claim: Rate lock-in is much weaker in the Sun Belt (Florida 25% at 6%+ vs 15% sub-3%; Tennessee ~27% vs 16%; Texas similar) than in California (27% sub-3% vs 16% at 6%+), which Gerli says explains why California, especially Southern California, has been slower to correct.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Sun Belt supply will keep rising faster; California's correction is delayed, not cancelled.

insights.claim: Sellers who bought in the last four years at 6-7% rates list more realistically because they don't treat a cheap mortgage as an extra asset, while sub-3% owners could stay in denial for another couple of years.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Price discovery will be led by recent buyers; watch the cohort of high-rate owners for distressed listings.

insights.claim: Homeowner equity is about $35 trillion, above GDP (~$30 trillion) and 2.5x the ~$14 trillion peak in 2006; Gerli argues that with normal sales volume and buyer demand prices would be 20-30% lower, so roughly that share of equity is 'phantom' sustained only by low liquidity.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Household wealth effects and HELOC-backed collateral are overstated; a normalized market implies a 20-30% repricing.
insights.quote: if we had a normal level of sales and buyer demand, prices would be down 20 to 30%.

insights.claim: Real (inflation-adjusted) US home prices were flat from 1890 to the late 1990s; Gerli says the market is now in a second bubble unsupported by income, rent or inflation, and dismisses bulls' use of home prices vs gold as irrelevant since houses are bought with wages and rents.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Long-run mean reversion argues against housing as a real-return asset class.

insights.claim: Buyer playbook: target listings sitting 4-6+ months that have already cut prices and ignore newly listed sellers; Gerli says he bought a house earlier in 2026 at $160k below its 2023 price and $110k below its 2021 price (25-35% below prior owners' purchase prices).
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Days-on-market and price-cut history are actionable signals of seller motivation for residential acquisitions.

insights.claim: Gerli calls the biggest unrecognized housing trend an AI-driven agglomeration back into 'legacy tier one' markets (New York, Chicago, San Francisco) with universities, Fortune 500 HQs and dense professional networks, while Sun Belt migration from the 2010s and the pandemic is over.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Reverses the remote-work real estate playbook; favors coastal/legacy metro residential and office over Sun Belt.
insights.quote: I think this is the biggest trend in housing that absolutely no one is talking about

insights.claim: Gerli argues AI is the counterweight to remote work: AI tools can replace many single-function remote roles (developer, copywriter, designer, analyst), and workers reinventing workflows with AI benefit from proximity to peers, pushing people back to big-city offices.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Supports office demand and urban rents in AI/finance hubs; negative for remote-work boomtowns.

insights.claim: RealPage data show top apartment rent growth in San Francisco (+14% YoY), San Jose (+9%), Virginia Beach (+6.5%), Oakland (+6.1%), Milwaukee (+4.5%), New York (+4%), West Palm Beach (+3.5%), Chicago (+2.8%), plus Cleveland and Detroit, while rents fall in San Antonio, Denver, Charlotte, Tampa, Houston, Phoenix, Nashville, Fort Worth, Dallas and Austin.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Rents are the cleanest real-time demand signal; multifamily exposure should tilt to Bay Area/Midwest/NY over Sun Belt.

insights.claim: New York metro still hosts 49 Fortune 500 headquarters, followed by Chicago 30, Houston 26, San Jose 21, DC 20, Dallas 19, Minneapolis 15, Atlanta 15, San Francisco 14, and Boston 14.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Corporate HQ density is Gerli's proxy for which metros win the AI-era migration.

insights.claim: Gerli expects a different set of real estate winners and losers over the next 5-7 years / decade than in the prior decade, with Sun Belt pandemic towns hurt by both continued new supply and a reduced relative advantage.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Signals a regime change in regional real estate allocation.

insights.claim: Gerli says if he had to pick one market to buy in now it would be Manhattan, arguing it is one of the most historically undervalued markets: prices fell ~10-12% nominally over 10 years (about -51% inflation-adjusted per his figures) while hotel rates and rents are surging.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Contrarian long on Manhattan residential after a decade-long real decline.
insights.quote: if I had to pick one market to buy in right now, it would be New York City. It would be Manhattan specifically

insights.claim: The Manhattan-to-US median home value multiple has fallen to 3.41, about half its 2010s level and the lowest since 2000, and Gerli would not be surprised if Manhattan is on the precipice of a multi-year boom given low inventory and corporate density.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Relative valuation suggests mean reversion upside for NYC property vs the national market.

insights.claim: Manhattan hotel rates for late October 2026 were ~$700-$1,000+ per night even for mid-tier Marriott brands (Courtyard ~$898, Residence Inn ~$899, Westin ~$857), which Gerli cites as evidence of intense demand.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Strong NYC hotel pricing supports lodging REIT/hotel operator exposure to Manhattan.

insights.claim: Some Manhattan co-ops/condos approach the 1% rule: e.g., a ~$399k studio (Zestimate $400k, down 23% in five years) renting for ~$3,900/month with ~$1,300 monthly fees, implying ~10-11% gross yields and 6%+ cap rates, rare in the US today.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Yield-based case for NYC small-unit investment, subject to building-level diligence.

insights.claim: Key risks to the Manhattan thesis are political (the current mayor and a left-leaning city council could expand rules such as the pied-a-terre tax) and building-level issues (underfunded reserves, special assessments for major systems), requiring review of property condition assessments and reserve schedules.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Policy and HOA/co-op reserve risk are the main underwriting hazards for NYC residential.

insights.claim: Inflation-adjusted 10-year value changes are also negative in DC (-26%), the Bronx (-27%) and San Francisco (-10%), so Gerli considers San Francisco still fairly undervalued despite its current boom.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Legacy metros that lagged in real terms may have room to run.

insights.claim: Reventure forecasts US deaths will exceed births by 2033-2034; a Mortgage Bankers Association white paper (covered by Bloomberg in July) puts the crossover at 2030 and warns elevated construction could push home prices lower.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Mainstream industry acknowledgment of a demographic housing glut is a structural headwind for home prices within a decade.

insights.claim: The US birth rate fell from 1.64% of population in 1991 (vs a 0.85% death rate) amid lower fertility and aging; 75+ year-olds will reach ~12% of the population by 2035 as boomers age, adding supply as mortality rises.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Aging-driven housing supply release is mathematically baked in.

insights.claim: Gerli highlights a two-sided squeeze: boomers aging into 75+ release supply while Gen X, about 20% smaller, provides ~20% fewer early-retirement (55-64) buyers over the next 10-15 years, a demand collapse in retirement destinations like Florida, Arizona, South Carolina and parts of Tennessee.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Retirement-destination housing faces simultaneous supply surge and buyer shortfall for 15 years.
insights.quote: Gen X is about 20% smaller than baby boomers.

insights.claim: Share of homeowners aged 75+ is highest in Hawaii (21.5%) and Florida (18.7%, up from 15.3% 20 years ago); in Naples, FL about 29% of homeowners are 75+, with North Port-Sarasota and Port St. Lucie also exposed, making Gerli structurally bearish on Florida.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Florida retirement-heavy metros carry the highest demographic supply risk.

insights.claim: Gerli's framework: the ratio of 25-44 year-old renter households to 75+ owner households gauges who will absorb aging owners' homes; nationally it fell from 2.2 (2013) to 1.7 (21M vs 12M), Florida is 1.14 (from 1.5 in 2015), Naples 0.35 (from 0.85 in 2005), West Virginia below 1, while Texas is 2.7, Austin 4.7 and California 2.5.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: A simple screen for long-run housing demand resilience; Gerli predicts it becomes a mainstream metric within five years.

insights.claim: Gerli says the only thing that could rescue home prices from demographic headwinds is 1970s-style multi-year double-digit inflation with 8-10% wage growth; with wages growing ~3% and decelerating, he expects cheaper or stagnating prices and poor real returns from housing over the next decade or two.
insights.speaker: Nick Gerli (Reventure Consulting)
insights.so_what: Housing as an investment likely underperforms absent an inflationary regime; inflation is the key risk to the bearish view.
